title: A majorization relation for a sum of two tensor products of positive semidefinite operators
abstract: We use linear programming to prove a separable version of Ky Fan's majorization relation for a sum of two operators that are each a tensor product of $n$ positive semidefinite operators. We give an example showing that such a relation does not hold in general for sums of three or more tensor products of three or more positive semidefinite operators.
summary: This theoretical paper proves a majorization relation concerning the sum of two operators, each being a tensor product of multiple positive semidefinite components. The proof utilizes advanced linear programming techniques applied to index set combinatorics. It advances the mathematical understanding of operator inequalities in high-dimensional quantum systems while also mapping out the precise limits where these relations break down.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove a separable version of Ky Fan's majorization relation for the sum of two operators, where each operator is constructed as a tensor product of multiple positive semidefinite (PSD) operators.
main_result: A specific majorization relation ($	ext{Theorem 1.1}$) is proven using linear programming techniques, although the authors also provide counterexamples showing that this relation fails for sums involving three or more tensor products.
method: The proof heavily relies on linear programming methods and establishing inequalities related to the dimensions of intersections between subspaces defined by downward-closed and upward-closed sets in product index spaces.
model_or_system: The mathematical framework involves operators acting on high-dimensional Hilbert spaces ($\mathbb{C}^{d_1 	imes \cdots 	imes d_n}$) that are structured as sums of tensor products of local PSD operators. This structure is relevant to analyzing quantum correlations or entanglement measures.
key_observables: The primary observables are the eigenvalues ($\lambda$) of the sum of projected operators, and the dimension of intersections between subspaces defined by index sets $\Omega$ and $\Upsilon$.
important_parameters: The number of tensor product factors ($n$), the number of summands (two in the main theorem), and the dimensions $d_i$ are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The proof technique is established for a specific case ($n=2$) using linear programming, and counterexamples demonstrate limitations when generalizing to more terms or factors.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the majorization problem ($	ext{Theorem 1.1}$), reduces it to an inequality involving projectors ($	ext{Theorem 1.2}$), and proves this latter theorem using combinatorial inequalities derived from properties of product spaces, culminating in counterexamples showing limitations.
why_interesting: Majorization relations are fundamental tools for comparing quantum states or operators (e.g., entanglement measures). Establishing such structural inequalities for tensor products is crucial for understanding multipartite quantum correlations and resource theories.
